 Advertisement Getty Images Abdelmawgood Samir 38 minutes ago Translated by Jesus vows to respond to the insult
 Share Follow GOAL on Google Jorge Jesus, the manager of the Portugal national team, was keen to send a message to the fans following the heavy defeat to Denmark 1-4, in the match that brought them together on Saturday evening at the Braga Municipal Stadium, as part of the UEFA Nations League, stressing the need to analyse the reasons behind the setback and correct the mistakes before the next encounter.
 Advertisement The Portuguese coach posted the message on his social media accounts after a defeat that cost his country the chance to seal top spot in their group. Portugal had gone into the game able to wrap up first place early. Instead, the decision now goes to the final round.
 Jesus admitted his side fell short against Denmark, but he refused to let one defeat define everything they had produced across the tournament, pointing to the results that had kept them top of the group.
 "We do not always achieve the results we want," the manager wrote. "Yesterday we were not at our best, but one match does not erase the work we have put in. Four wins in five matches, and we are still top of the group."
 He added: "We win and lose together. Now it is time to analyse, correct and continue working, united and determined to achieve our goals."
 Advertisement Advertisement His words back the work of the previous matches while owning the shortfall against Denmark. The next stage, he knows, demands a hard look at what went wrong.

 Wales clash will decide top spot 
 Portugal are back in action on Tuesday, travelling to Cardiff to face Wales in a game they must take points from to guarantee first place in the group.
 Advertisement They will not travel at full strength. João Palhinha and Rúben Dias are both suspended, while Bernardo Silva is out injured, leaving the coaching staff to juggle three absences before a decisive clash.
 Settling the group against Denmark was the plan. A four-goal-to-one defeat put paid to that, forcing Portugal to wait until the final round and leaving top spot hanging on the Wales result.
 Advertisement Jesus is expected to dissect the Denmark display in the build-up and pick apart the mistakes that cost them, before a final test in which Portugal aim to confirm top spot and sign off from the group in a very different fashion to their showing in Braga.

 My story with soccer began when I was just a toddler, a little boy who didn’t fully understand what he was watching, but the magic emanating from the fields was too powerful to resist. I clearly remember following the Egyptian national team at the 1990 World Cup in Italy, where my eyes were filled with wonder at the dramatic moments, and my heart was immersed in a sea of endless excitement. That was the beginning, the spark that ignited a passion that still burns today.
 In the vault of my sporting memories, there are moments that will never fade. But if I had to choose just one, it would undoubtedly be Zinedine Zidane’s immortal goal in the 2002 Champions League final against Bayer Leverkusen. A single ball, a rocket from “Zizou’s” left foot, flew in a mesmerizing arc to find the back of the net, securing Real Madrid’s ninth title. It was a moment when time stood still—a blend of beauty and power—reminding us that soccer is not just a game, but an art that touches the soul.
 As for my all-time favorite lineup? It’s really tough—it’s like choosing among the stars in the sky. Here it is: (Goalkeeper) Gianluigi Buffon… (Defense): Roberto Carlos, Cafu, Alessandro Nesta, Paolo Maldini… (Midfield): Zinedine Zidane, Claude Makélélé, Lionel Messi, Andrés Iniesta... (Forward): Cristiano Ronaldo, Ronaldo “The Phenomenon.”
